main_text.p: evicimus humores illos, videlicet bi-dem & succum pancreaticum, rectè dictos fuisse dispositione subcontraria affectos. An vero subcontrariorum illorum humorum permixtione in il-lis oriatur effervescentia discutiendum suscipit Le Vasseur pag. 10. ubi chartam diris & puerilibus implens exe-crationibus exclamat Dii Vostram fi-dem! & quæ præterea sunt maniæ illius symptomata quæ illi ignoscenda, supra monitum; sed ante omnia examinandum, an Le Vasseur intelligat quid sit effervescentia, quam tanto molimine negat. Doctor igitur noster nominalis derivat effervescentiam [?] ab igne, eam vocans [?] pag. 6. [?] pag. 10. unde effervescentiam frigori non modo opponit, pag. 25. his verbis frigore nequaquam densari hoc phlegma; quod tamen necesse est si effervescentiâ liquetur: Quâ de re latius suo loco: Sed etiam vi nominis, uti solent rerum ignari,

page.notes: The Greek words (after "derivat effervescentiam", "vocans", and the "pag. 6." and "pag. 10." references) are only partly legible at this scan resolution; they are marked [?] and should be checked against the original. Catchword "ignari," is set at the right below the last full line. The first line is a fragment continuing from the previous page. Printed "65" is read from a worn numeral.
